title: Candidate Failover Policy Evaluation — Arch Review Notes
summary: Architecture review focused on three candidate failover policies for production routing: (A) Regional-first model-variant fallback, (B) Cost-priority routing with quantized variants, and (C) Graceful-degradation via degraded responses + client hints. We walked through evaluation results from the staged canary (region eu-west-1 and us-east-1), discussed SLO impact, rollback behavior, observability gaps, and operational runbooks.
discussion_points: Overview of the three policy candidates and expected behavior under capacity pressure
Canary experiment setup: 5% traffic in eu-west-1, 2% in us-east-1; traffic mix synthetic + real low-volume customer traffic
Observed p95/p99 latency delta when switching to quantized variants (candidate B): +18ms p95, +65ms p99 on long-context requests (>1024 tokens)
Model-quality regressions measured with prompt-set A: mean rouge-like score drop 1.8% for 4-bit quantized variant; some failure modes in math/formatting prompts
Operational complexity tradeoffs: region-first requires stateful session affinity awareness; cost-priority requires dynamic price table + billing alignment
Fallback amplification risk: simultaneous multi-tenant failover causing cascade to lower tier models — need tenant QoS credits
Observability: missing per-decision tracing tag for 'failover-reason' (capacity | error | perf | policy) — blocks postmortems and automation
Rollout mechanics: prefer progressive windowed canaries with automatic rollback on SLO breach, + manual gating for model-quality alerts
decisions: Adopt hybrid policy: region-first primary with model-variant fallback (candidate A augmented with candidate B), i.e., attempt same-region variants -> cross-region same-tier -> quantized variant -> degraded response
Implement a per-tenant QoS credit system to limit cascade effects; SRE to own credit throttler implementation
Add a 'failover-reason' enumerable tag to all routing decisions and emit to request traces and metrics (priority: high)
Canary rollout plan approved: 1% global traffic -> 5% after 24h with no SLO breach -> 15% after 72h -> full. Auto rollback on >0.5% error increase or >5% p99 latency regression over baseline
Delay unlocking cost-priority (candidate B as standalone) until we have invoicing alignment and per-token cost telemetry; canary B as part of hybrid path only

experimental_results: Canary run (eu-west-1 5% traffic): baseline p99=420ms, hybrid-path p99=485ms (+15.5%)
Quantized variant standalone: mean token throughput +12%, but observed 1.8% quality drop on eval set A
Failure injection: simulated node outage in eu-west-1 resulted in 9% of sessions triggering cross-region fallback; without QoS credits, 4 tenants experienced cascading degradation
Cold-cache penalty: cross-region fallback adds average 120ms cold-start on first request due to KV cache warm-up
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions for specialized prompts when hitting quantized variants — Mitigation: hold critical customers on pinned variants; add per-prompt eval gating
Risk: Billing mismatch if cost-priority routes generate unexpected charges — Mitigation: require finance sign-off and implement per-variant chargeback simulation
Risk: Observability gap prevents fast diagnosis — Mitigation: urgent instrumentation work (failover-reason tag) and a short postmortem template
Risk: Tenant cascade during large outage — Mitigation: implement QoS credits + emergency cap per-tenant
unresolved_questions: Should degraded responses include a standard client hint for best-effort retry semantics (e.g., 'approximate=true')?
How to surface model-quality tradeoffs to customers in a transparent way (UI + API)?
What cost thresholds should automatically favour quantized variants for non-SLA traffic?
